 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR FINAL HEARING, THIS DAY, THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT

This appeal is filed challenging the judgment and award dated 15.12.2012 passed in M.V.C.
No.751/2010 by the Court of Fast Track-III & Addl. M.A.C.T at Tumkur (hereinafter referred as 'Tribunal').
2.

sentences.text: The parties are referred to as per their rank before the Tribunal for the sake of convenience.

3. The relevant facts necessary for consideration of the present appeal are that, on 10.12.2009, the 1st respondent/claimant was alleged to be traveling in a motor cycle bearing No.KA-44 E 1573, at which time, another motor cycle bearing No.KA-44 H 4426 came from the opposite side NC:
2024:KHC:2366 and hit the claimant, when a tractor/trailer bearing No.KA-06 T 218/219 came in a high speed in a rash and negligent manner and hit against the petitioner causing the accident in question wherein, the claimant suffered grievous injuries.

Claiming compensation for the same, a claimant filed the claim petition before the Tribunal arraying the owner of the motor cycle bearing KA-44 H 4426 of respondent No.1 and the owner of the tractor/trailer as respondent No.2.
Subsequently, pursuant to an application filed by the claimant, the 3rd respondent before the Tribunal was impleaded on the ground that he was the purchaser of the tractor.

4. The claim proceedings was contested by the 3rd respondent by filing statement of objections wherein, it was contended that the accident has occurred due to the negligence caused by both the motor cycles and that the case against the driver of the tractor/trailer has been filed due to collusion with the Police Authorities.
Further, various grounds denying the nature of the injuries and the amounts spent by the claimant for the treatment have been taken by the 3rd respondent in the statement of objections.

NC: 2024:KHC:2366 Ramarao vs Channappa on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61722949/
2 5.
Consequent to the pleading of the parties, the claimant examined himself as PW.1 and marked Exs.P1 to P7.
No oral or documentary evidence has been produced by the respondents.

The Tribunal,
by its judgment and award dated 15.12.2012, allowed the claim petition and awarded compensation of `88,000/- together with interest @ 6% per annum and directed the 3rd respondent to pay the compensation awarded.
Being aggrieved, the 3rd respondent has filed the above appeal.
6. Along with the above appeal, I.A.No.2/2013 has been filed under Order XLI Rule 27 read with Section 151 of the Code of Civil Procedure to permit the appellant to lead additional evidence.
Along with the said application, the certified copy of the 'B' Extract of the tractor/trailer and notarized copy of the RC Book has been produced.

7. The learned counsel for the appellant submits that the appellant who is arrayed as the 3rd respondent before the Tribunal purchased the tractor/trailer which was transferred in his name on 23.01.2010.

Since the appellant subsequently purchased the vehicle in question after the date of the accident NC: 2024:KHC:2366 which has occurred on 12.10.2009, the 3rd respondent is not liable to pay the compensation awarded.
Hence, he submits that I.A.No.2/2013 be allowed and the appeal also be allowed.
8. Learned counsel for the appellant further submits that the quantum of compensation is excessive and hence, seeks for allowing the above appeal.

9. Per contra, learned counsel for the 1st respondent/claimant vehemently opposes the above application and submits that the appellant who is arrayed as 3rd respondent before the Tribunal did not take said contention that he subsequently purchased the vehicle before the Tribunal and hence,
no ground is made out to allow I.A.No.2/2013.
He further submits that the compensation is on the lower side and hence, seeks for dismissal of the above appeal.
10. The submissions of both the learned counsel have been considered and material on record have been perused including the records of the Tribunal.

The question that arises for consideration is:
NC: 2024:KHC:2366 (i) Whether I.A.No.2/2013 filed under Order XLI Rule 27 r/w Section 151 of IPC is liable to be allowed?
(ii) Whether the quantum of compensation awarded is excessive?

Regarding question (i):
11. I.A.No.2/2013 is filed under Order XLI Rule 27 r/w Section 151 of CPC, that the parties shall not be entitled to produce additional evidence.

However, an exception is made wherein, if the trial Court has refused to admit evidence which ought to have admitted or whether the party seeking to produce additional evidence, establishes that notwithstanding the exercise of due diligence, such evidence was not within his knowledge or he could not, after exercise of due diligence, produced such Ramarao vs Channappa on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61722949/
3 additional evidence, he will be permitted to produce additional evidence before the appellate Court.
12.

It is forthcoming from the affidavit filed in support of I.A.No.2/2013 that the appellant has not stated as to why the documents produced along with the said application could not have been produced before the Tribunal.
It is relevant to note that the appellant, who was arrayed as the 3rd respondent before the Tribunal, had entered appearance and filed his statement of objections to the claim petition.
In the said statement of objections the appellant has not even taken plea that he was not the owner of the vehicle as on the date of the accident.

Hence, the appellant not even having taken a plea in the statement of objections filed before the Tribunal that he is not the owner of the vehicle on the date of the accident and having regard to the averments made in the affidavit accompanying I.A.No.2/2013 has failed in satisfying the requisite criteria entitling him to invoke Order XLI Rule 27 r/w Section 151 of CPC.
The appellant has miserably failed in demonstrating that the relief sought for in I.A.No.2/2013 is required to be granted.
Hence, I.A.No.2/2013 is rejected.
The question (i) framed for consideration is answered in negative.

Regarding question (ii):
14.

With regard to the quantum of compensation, it is forthcoming that the claimant has produced the Wound NC: 2024:KHC:2366 Certificate (Ex.P3) which demonstrates that he has sustained compound fracture of both bones of right leg and the said injuries are grievous in nature.
The claimant has not produced any other documents to demonstrate the nature of treatment that he has taken for treatment of the said injuries.

The claimant has produced a bill dated 18.01.2010 (Ex.P7)
which is issued by "Zen Ortho" which discloses that a sum of `8,495/- has been incurred for purchase of various medical materials.
It is forthcoming that the said bill is computerized.

However,
the name of the claimant is handwritten.
The claimant has not adduced the evidence of Doctor.
Further, the nature of treatment undertaken by PW.1 is not stated and no evidence is adduced with regard to the same.
The claimant has stated that he was shifted to the Government Hospital at Tiptur and admitted as inpatient.
However, no documents have been produced regarding the same.
In view of the same, Ex.P7- medical bill cannot be considered for the purpose of assessing the compensation.

15. The Tribunal, while considering the quantum of compensation all though noticed that he has not adduced the NC: 2024:KHC:2366 evidence of the Doctor, looking at the injuries sustained, has awarded the compensation of `88,000/- on the following heads:
1. Pain and Agony `30,000.00/-

Medical Expenses and incidental 2. expenses `15,000.00/-
Ramarao vs Channappa on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/61722949/
4

Loss of Income during treatment period 3. (3000 X 6) `18,000.00/-
 Loss of Amenities and future 4. unhappiness `25,000.00/-
 TOTAL `88,000.00/-
 [
16.
However, it is relevant to note that there is no material to award medical expenses as also to award compensation on the other heads.

Hence, having regard to the fact that he sustained fracture of both bones of the right leg by taking into consideration the various heads of compensation it is just and proper that the compensation that is payable to claimant be reassessed in a lump sum of `50,000/-.
Accordingly, the compensation awarded by the Tribunal is - 10 - NC: 2024:KHC:2366 reduced from `88,000/- to `50,000/-.
The question No.(ii)
is answered accordingly.
